paras.text: Identify the correct intonation pattern in the following sentences:
paras.urdu: درج ذیل جملوں میں لہجے کا درست انداز پہچانیں:
paras.pashto: په لاندې جملو کې د اهنګ سمه بڼه وپېژنئ:

paras.text: 1. You already!
paras.urdu: 1. You already! — (تم پہلے ہی!)
paras.pashto: 1. You already! — (ته دمخه!)

paras.text: 2. You shouldn't have.
paras.urdu: 2. You shouldn't have. — (تمہیں ایسا نہیں کرنا چاہیے تھا۔)
paras.pashto: 2. You shouldn't have. — (تا باید داسې نه وای کړي.)

paras.text: 3. It's unbelievable!
paras.urdu: 3. It's unbelievable! — (ناقابلِ یقین ہے!)
paras.pashto: 3. It's unbelievable! — (د باور وړ نه ده!)

paras.text: 4. That's not very nice!
paras.urdu: 4. That's not very nice! — (یہ زیادہ اچھا نہیں!)
paras.pashto: 4. That's not very nice! — (دا ډېره ښه نه ده!)

paras.text: 5. I don't think I will.
paras.urdu: 5. I don't think I will. — (میرا نہیں خیال کہ میں کروں گا۔)
paras.pashto: 5. I don't think I will. — (فکر نه کوم چې وبه یې کړم.)

paras.text: 6. How could you?
paras.urdu: 6. How could you? — (تم ایسا کیسے کر سکتے ہو؟)
paras.pashto: 6. How could you? — (ته دا څنګه کولی شې؟)

paras.text: 7. Why should I tell you?
paras.urdu: 7. Why should I tell you? — (میں تمہیں کیوں بتاؤں؟)
paras.pashto: 7. Why should I tell you? — (ولې درته ووایم؟)

paras.text: 8. You must be joking!
paras.urdu: 8. You must be joking! — (تم مذاق کر رہے ہو!)
paras.pashto: 8. You must be joking! — (ته ټوکې کوې!)

paras.text: 9. So what?
paras.urdu: 9. So what? — (تو کیا ہوا؟)
paras.pashto: 9. So what? — (نو څه؟)

paras.text: 10. Well, I never!
paras.urdu: 10. Well, I never! — (اچھا، کبھی نہیں سنا!)
paras.pashto: 10. Well, I never! — (ښه، هېڅکله!)

paras.text: 11. You know best, don't you?
paras.urdu: 11. You know best, don't you? — (تم بہتر جانتے ہو، ہے نا؟)
paras.pashto: 11. You know best, don't you? — (ته ښه پوهېږې، داسې نه ده؟)

paras.text: 12. How do you do?
paras.urdu: 12. How do you do? — (آپ کیسے ہیں؟)
paras.pashto: 12. How do you do? — (څنګه یاست؟)

paras.text: 13. How long have you been building flutes?
paras.urdu: 13. How long have you been building flutes? — (آپ کب سے بانسریاں بنا رہے ہیں؟)
paras.pashto: 13. How long have you been building flutes? — (څومره وخت کېږي چې شپېلۍ جوړوئ؟)

paras.text: 14. Can I see one of your flutes?
paras.urdu: 14. Can I see one of your flutes? — (کیا میں آپ کی ایک بانسری دیکھ سکتا ہوں؟)
paras.pashto: 14. Can I see one of your flutes? — (ایا ستاسو یوه شپېلۍ لیدلی شم؟)

paras.text: 15. Is this your flute?
paras.urdu: 15. Is this your flute? — (کیا یہ آپ کی بانسری ہے؟)
paras.pashto: 15. Is this your flute? — (ایا دا ستاسو شپېلۍ ده؟)

paras.text: D. Noun Phrases
paras.urdu: D. اسمی فقرے
paras.pashto: D. نومي عبارتونه

paras.text: A noun phrase is a group of words that serves the same purpose as a noun. A noun phrase can be the subject or object of a verb.It can also be the object of a preposition.
paras.urdu: اسمی فقرہ الفاظ کا ایسا گروہ ہے جو اسم کا کام کرتا ہے۔ اسمی فقرہ فعل کا فاعل یا مفعول ہو سکتا ہے۔ یہ حرفِ جار کا مفعول بھی ہو سکتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: نومي عبارت د کلمو داسې ډله ده چې د نوم کار کوي. نومي عبارت د فعل فاعل یا مفعول کېدای شي. د اضافې مفعول هم کېدای شي.

paras.text: Examples :
paras.urdu: مثالیں:
paras.pashto: بېلګې:

paras.text: I hope to stand first in the class. [underlined: to stand first in the class]
paras.urdu: I hope to stand first in the class. [خط کشیدہ: to stand first in the class]
paras.pashto: I hope to stand first in the class. [لاندې کرښه: to stand first in the class]

paras.text: He wished to talk to his teacher. [underlined: to talk to his teacher]
paras.urdu: He wished to talk to his teacher. [خط کشیدہ: to talk to his teacher]
paras.pashto: He wished to talk to his teacher. [لاندې کرښه: to talk to his teacher]

paras.text: The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed. [underlined: to pay back every penny he owed]
paras.urdu: The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed. [خط کشیدہ: to pay back every penny he owed]
paras.pashto: The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed. [لاندې کرښه: to pay back every penny he owed]

paras.text: Horses prefer living in dark stables. [underlined: living in dark stables]
paras.urdu: Horses prefer living in dark stables. [خط کشیدہ: living in dark stables]
paras.pashto: Horses prefer living in dark stables. [لاندې کرښه: living in dark stables]

paras.text: Have you ever tried to climb a tree? [underlined: to climb a tree]
paras.urdu: Have you ever tried to climb a tree? [خط کشیدہ: to climb a tree]
paras.pashto: Have you ever tried to climb a tree? [لاندې کرښه: to climb a tree]

paras.text: Dont touch those books. [underlined: touch those books]
paras.urdu: Dont touch those books. [خط کشیدہ: touch those books]
paras.pashto: Dont touch those books. [لاندې کرښه: touch those books]

paras.text: She came with her older sister. [underlined: with her older sister]
paras.urdu: She came with her older sister. [خط کشیدہ: with her older sister]
paras.pashto: She came with her older sister. [لاندې کرښه: with her older sister]

paras.text: She gave him a big sweet piece of cake. [underlined: him a big sweet piece of cake]
paras.urdu: She gave him a big sweet piece of cake. [خط کشیدہ: him a big sweet piece of cake]
paras.pashto: She gave him a big sweet piece of cake. [لاندې کرښه: him a big sweet piece of cake]

paras.text: They are both excellent teachers. [underlined: both excellent teachers]
paras.urdu: They are both excellent teachers. [خط کشیدہ: both excellent teachers]
paras.pashto: They are both excellent teachers. [لاندې کرښه: both excellent teachers]

paras.text: All the underlined group of words in the above sentences are noun phrases.
paras.urdu: مندرجہ بالا جملوں میں تمام خط کشیدہ الفاظ کے گروہ اسمی فقرے ہیں۔

paras.text: THE HEAD of a noun phrase is the noun being described or referred to in the phrase:
paras.urdu: اسمی فقرے کا ’’سر‘‘ (HEAD) وہ اسم ہے جس کی فقرے میں صفت بیان کی جا رہی ہو یا جس کا حوالہ دیا جا رہا ہو:

paras.text: Sometimes a pronoun can be the head of a noun phrase:
paras.urdu: کبھی کبھی ضمیر بھی اسمی فقرے کا سر ہو سکتا ہے:

paras.urdu: They both know the truth — (وہ دونوں سچ جانتے ہیں)
paras.pashto: They both know the truth — (دوی دواړه رښتیا پېژني)

paras.text: Are all this for me?
paras.urdu: Are all this for me? — (کیا یہ سب میرے لیے ہے؟)
paras.pashto: Are all this for me? — (ایا دا ټول زما لپاره دي؟)

paras.text: Have you anything new to tell me?
paras.urdu: Have you anything new to tell me? — (کیا تمہارے پاس مجھے بتانے کو کچھ نیا ہے؟)
paras.pashto: Have you anything new to tell me? — (ایا ماته د ویلو لپاره څه نوي لرې؟)

D. Noun Phrases

A noun phrase is a group of words that serves the same purpose as a noun. A noun phrase can be the subject or object of a verb.It can also be the object of a preposition.

Examples :

I hope to stand first in the class. [underlined: to stand first in the class]

He wished to talk to his teacher. [underlined: to talk to his teacher]

The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed. [underlined: to pay back every penny he owed]

Horses prefer living in dark stables. [underlined: living in dark stables]

Have you ever tried to climb a tree? [underlined: to climb a tree]

Dont touch those books. [underlined: touch those books]

She came with her older sister. [underlined: with her older sister]

She gave him a big sweet piece of cake. [underlined: him a big sweet piece of cake]

They are both excellent teachers. [underlined: both excellent teachers]

All the underlined group of words in the above sentences are noun phrases.

THE HEAD of a noun phrase is the noun being described or referred to in the phrase:

For example,

Her older sister

A big piece of cake

Many pleasant days

Sometimes a pronoun can be the head of a noun phrase:

That's a big one

I would like those read ones

They both know the truth

Are all this for me?

Have you anything new to tell me?

sections.content:
Identify the correct intonation pattern in the following sentences:

1. You already!

2. You shouldn't have.

3. It's unbelievable!

4. That's not very nice!

5. I don't think I will.

6. How could you?

7. Why should I tell you?

8. You must be joking!

9. So what?

10. Well, I never!

11. You know best, don't you?

12. How do you do?

13. How long have you been building flutes?

14. Can I see one of your flutes?

15. Is this your flute?

D. Noun Phrases

A noun phrase is a group of words that serves the same purpose as a noun. A noun phrase can be the subject or object of a verb.It can also be the object of a preposition.

Examples :

I hope to stand first in the class. [underlined: to stand first in the class]

He wished to talk to his teacher. [underlined: to talk to his teacher]

The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed. [underlined: to pay back every penny he owed]

Horses prefer living in dark stables. [underlined: living in dark stables]

Have you ever tried to climb a tree? [underlined: to climb a tree]

Dont touch those books. [underlined: touch those books]

She came with her older sister. [underlined: with her older sister]

She gave him a big sweet piece of cake. [underlined: him a big sweet piece of cake]

They are both excellent teachers. [underlined: both excellent teachers]

All the underlined group of words in the above sentences are noun phrases.

THE HEAD of a noun phrase is the noun being described or referred to in the phrase:

For example,

Her older sister

A big piece of cake

Many pleasant days

Sometimes a pronoun can be the head of a noun phrase:

That's a big one

I would like those read ones

They both know the truth

Are all this for me?

Have you anything new to tell me?

Activity

12. He is such a kind man.

13. They are in the back garden.
